title: Paula Blasi wins Vuelta Espana Feminina after historic Alto de l’Angliru climb
content:
Paula Blasi has won the 2026 Vuelta Espana Feminina with a historic solo ride on the Alto de l’Angliru on Saturday.

Blasi, 23 — who only joined UAE Team ADQ last year — finished second on the 132.9 kilometer deciding stage, having dropped the race leader Anna van der Breggen on the final climb, to top the general classification by 24 seconds.

The Spaniard also collected the queen of the mountains jersey, while Lotte Kopecky finished with the points jersey and Marion Bunel was crowned best young rider.

Saturday was the first time ever that the women’s professional peloton has scaled the famous 12.4 kilometer Angliru — where Joao Almeida held off Jonas Vingegaard in September’s men’s race — which boasts a fearsome average gradient of 9.7 per cent but reaches up to 23 per cent.

It marked Blasi’s second win of an impressive year, after a shock Amstel Gold triumph in the spring season, and she was joined on the podium by Van der Breggen and Marion Bunel, 21.

Stiasni, 24, took the win on the day by 23 seconds, having only had only one professional win to her name going into Saturday’s stage — last year’s Grand Prix Boquerón nine-kilometer time trial. She was part of a small group that caught a breakaway of Riejanne Markus (Lidl – Trek), Femke Markus (SD Worx – Protime) and Liane Lippert (Movistar) on the Angliru.

SD Worx’s Anna van der Breggen entered the final stage leading the GC after a strong stage win the day before, riding everyone off the wheel in the final climb to gain an 18 second gap. Blasi had finished eight seconds behind her, as the only one who could match the 36-year-old’s acceleration.

Everything was to play for, however, with the top 20 in the GC within three minutes of each other heading into the stage, and five riders within one minute of each other.

Analysis by Jacob Whitehead

Blasi’s rise has been meteoric. Last year was the former duathlete’s first year with a professional squad, spending most of it with UAE’s development team. There were no signs she would be this good, this soon — she finished sixth at the 2025 Tour de l’Avenir behind riders who have not even begun to imprint their tiremarks at this level.

The Ardennes campaign was the first real sign of her development — catapulting her into the ‘it girl’ of world cycling after taking a shock victory at Amstel Gold, a race she was not even supposed to enter, but for team illness. There, as the last survivor of the breakaway, she held off fast-charging stars Demi Vollering and Kasia Niewadoma-Phinney to earn a solo win. Subsequent top five finishes at Fleche Wallone and Liege-Bastogne-Liege showed this result was no fluke.

Victory at La Vuelta, however, and to seal it on the fearsome Angliru? This was not just another step — it was a leap into cycling’s true elite.

Already, Blasi has shown the ability to win across multiple terrains — she can time trial too — and as a Grand Tour winner at the age of 23, there are now few races which she is not now a genuine contender to win. Vollering remains the season’s outstanding rider, but it is now only right to include Blasi on the tier below, on this form at least, alongside the likes of Niewadoma-Phinney and Pauline Ferrand-Prevot, both defeated here.
